title: Pistachio-crusted salmon
intro: Tender salmon under a crunchy pistachio and lemon zest crust.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.

airfryer.t: Preheat the air fryer to 180°C and line the basket with perforated baking paper.

steps.t: Roughly chop the pistachios and mix with the grated lemon zest, parsley, oil, salt and pepper.
Pat the salmon dry, lay it skin side down on the tray and season lightly with salt.
Press the pistachio crust firmly onto the top of the fillets.
Bake until the salmon flakes easily and the crust is golden, 52-55°C in the centre.
steps.label: Oven

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 180°C for 10 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily.

steps.t: Let it rest, squeeze over the lemon juice and serve.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Chop the pistachios by hand, not in a blender: uneven pieces stay crunchier.
Serve with a fennel and orange salad.

title: Sea bass en papillote
intro: Whole sea bass steamed in its parcel with cherry tomatoes, olives and capers.

ing.n: whole sea bass, gutted, about 400 g each

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C. Rinse the fish and pat dry inside and out.

bbq.t: Set up the barbecue for indirect cooking at about 200°C. Rinse the fish and pat dry.

steps.t: Salt the cavity and fill it with lemon slices, sliced garlic and parsley.
Lay each fish on a large sheet of baking paper and scatter halved tomatoes, olives and capers around it.
Drizzle with oil and wine, then seal the parcels by tightly folding the edges.
Bake until the flesh comes away easily from the backbone.
steps.label: Oven

bbq.t: Use foil instead of paper and cook over indirect heat with the lid closed for 22 minutes.

steps.t: Open the parcels at the table, fillet the fish and serve with its juices.

tips.t: The parcel is ready when it puffs up: open it at the table so the aroma hits everyone.
Serve with boiled potatoes dressed with olive oil and parsley.

title: Mussels marinara
intro: Mussels steamed open over high heat with garlic, wine, cherry tomatoes and parsley.

steps.t: Rinse the mussels in cold water, pull off the beards and scrub the shells; discard open ones that don't close when tapped.
In a wide pot, heat the oil with crushed garlic and the chilli over medium heat until the garlic sizzles.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook until they soften.
steps.label: Tomatoes

steps.t: Tip in the mussels and wine, cover and cook over high heat, shaking the pot, until they open.
steps.label: Mussels

steps.t: Discard any that stay closed, add parsley and pepper and toss well.
Serve at once in deep bowls with all the juices.

tips.t: Don't add salt: the liquid the mussels release is salty enough.
Shelled, with the strained juices, they dress 320 g spaghetti the same day.
Leave out the tomatoes, just garlic, wine and parsley, for a lighter version.

title: Gambas al ajillo
intro: Prawns sizzling in garlic and chilli olive oil, straight from the tapas bar.

steps.t: Pat the prawns very dry with kitchen paper and salt them lightly.
Thinly slice the garlic and crumble the chilli.
In a small clay dish or frying pan, heat the oil with the garlic and chilli over medium-low heat until the garlic is barely golden.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Turn up the heat, add the prawns and cook, stirring, until pink and opaque.
steps.label: Prawns

steps.t: Turn off the heat, add the paprika and parsley and serve right away in the pan, still sizzling.

tips.t: Don't let the garlic brown: once it turns dark, the oil tastes bitter.
Put crusty bread on the table for the oil, and a glass of chilled white wine.

title: Baccalà alla vicentina
intro: Stockfish cooked for hours in milk and olive oil until meltingly soft.

steps.t: Open the stockfish, remove the backbone and pin bones, keep the skin on and cut it into 6-7 cm pieces.
Thinly slice the onions and cook them in 100 ml oil over low heat until soft; add the anchovies and let them melt.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Mix the flour, Parmigiano, parsley, salt and pepper; coat the pieces, fill them with a little onion and close them up.
Arrange the pieces skin side down in a wide pan, side by side, and cover with the rest of the onions.
Pour in the milk and the remaining oil until the fish is covered.
Cook over the lowest heat without stirring: it should barely tremble. Shake the pan now and then.
steps.label: Slow cook

steps.t: Turn off the heat and let it rest: the sauce thickens and the fish absorbs the flavour.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve hot with soft or grilled polenta.

tips.t: Never stir: shake the pan instead, so the pieces stay whole.
Rested overnight in the fridge it's even better: reheat over very low heat.
In Vicenza it's served with white polenta.

title: Teriyaki salmon
intro: Crisp-skinned salmon lacquered in a glossy soy and mirin glaze.

steps.t: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Pat the salmon dry and place it skin side down in a non-stick pan with the oil over medium heat.
Cook until the skin is crisp and the salmon is opaque two thirds of the way up.
steps.label: Skin

steps.t: Turn it over and cook the other side.
steps.label: Second side

steps.t: Blot off excess fat with kitchen paper, pour in the sauce and simmer, spooning it over the fish, until glossy.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.t: Serve with rice, sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.

tips.t: Blot the fat out of the pan before adding the sauce, or the glaze won't cling.
Serve with Japanese rice and blanched spinach dressed with sesame.
With boneless chicken thighs: 6 minutes per side, until 75°C in the centre.

title: Fish moqueca
intro: Brazilian layered fish stew with peppers, tomato and coconut milk.

steps.t: Cut the fish into chunks, season with the lime juice, crushed garlic, salt and pepper and put it in the fridge.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile, thinly slice the onion, peppers and tomatoes into rings.
In a wide casserole, warm the oil with the paprika and layer in half the vegetables.
Lay the fish and its marinade on top and cover with the rest of the vegetables.
Pour in the coconut milk, cover and cook over medium-low heat until the fish is opaque and flakes.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Uncover, check the salt and cook a little longer to thicken the sauce.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Turn off the heat, scatter with coriander and serve with white rice.

tips.t: Don't stir: just shake the pot so the fish stays in pieces.
Half fish, half peeled prawns: add the prawns for the last 5 minutes.
Serve with white rice and farofa, toasted cassava flour.

title: Sole meunière
intro: Floured, golden sole served with brown butter, lemon and parsley.

ing.n: whole skinned sole, about 300 g each

steps.t: Pat the sole dry, season with salt and pepper, then flour them and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil and 20 g butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until the butter foams.
Cook the sole dark side down until golden.
steps.label: First side

steps.t: Turn carefully and cook the other side until the flesh lifts off the bone.
steps.label: Second side

steps.t: Move them to warm plates and wipe out the pan with kitchen paper.
Melt the rest of the butter until nutty brown and fragrant, then turn off the heat and add half the lemon's juice and the parsley.
steps.label: Brown butter

steps.t: Spoon the butter over the sole and serve with lemon wedges.

tips.t: Flour at the last moment: if the flour turns damp, the sole won't brown.
Serve with parsley potatoes or buttered spinach.

title: Swordfish alla ghiotta
intro: Swordfish steaks cooked in a Sicilian sauce of olives, capers and raisins.

steps.t: Soak the raisins in warm water, then squeeze them dry.
steps.label: Raisins

steps.t: Meanwhile, fry the chopped onion and celery in the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until soft.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Add the halved tomatoes, olives, capers, pine nuts and raisins; salt lightly and cook until the sauce reduces.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Lay the swordfish in the sauce, cover and cook the first side.
steps.label: First side

steps.t: Turn the steaks and cook until just opaque in the centre but still moist.
steps.label: Second side

steps.t: Turn off the heat, add torn basil and pepper and serve with the sauce.

tips.t: Don't overcook it: take it off as soon as it's opaque in the centre, or swordfish turns dry.
Flake any leftover fish into the sauce and toss it with pasta the next day.

title: Octopus alla luciana
intro: Octopus cooked slowly in its own tomato, olive and caper sauce until tender.

steps.t: In a deep pot, ideally earthenware, heat the oil with crushed garlic and chilli over medium heat.
Add the crushed tomatoes, olives and capers and cook for a few minutes.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Lay the whole octopus in the sauce, cover with a heavy lid and cook over the lowest heat without adding water.
steps.label: Octopus

pressure.t: Pressure cooker: lay the octopus in the sauce, lock the lid and cook 20 minutes at high pressure, then release.

steps.t: Pierce the thickest part with a fork: if it slides in easily it's done, otherwise cook 10 minutes more.
Turn off the heat and let the octopus rest covered in its sauce: it gets even more tender.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Cut the octopus into pieces, return it to the sauce, sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

tips.t: Don't salt: the octopus releases its own salty juices and seasons the sauce.
Serve with slices of toasted country bread (gluten-free if needed).
Leftover sauce makes a great dressing for linguine the next day.

title: Peruvian ceviche
intro: Raw fish cured for minutes in lime, with red onion, sweet potato and corn.

ing.n: very fresh white fish (sea bass, bream)

steps.t: The fish must be very fresh and blast-frozen: at home, freeze it for at least 96 hours at -18 °C and thaw it in the fridge.
Boil the whole sweet potatoes in their skins in salted water until a knife slides in easily.
steps.label: Sweet potatoes

steps.t: Meanwhile boil the corn cobs (3 minutes is enough if pre-cooked), then cut them into thick rounds.
steps.label: Corn

steps.t: Slice the red onion paper-thin and drop it into iced water: it loses its harshness and stays crisp.
Cut the fish into 2 cm cubes, put them in a cold bowl and keep in the fridge. Seed the chili and chop it finely.
Squeeze the limes by hand without pressing too hard, and strain the juice.
Salt the fish, add grated garlic and the chili, cover with the lime juice and 2 ice cubes, and stir gently.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Remove the ice, add the drained onion and chopped cilantro and check the salt: the fish should be opaque outside, raw inside.
Peel and slice the sweet potatoes and serve the ceviche at once with them and the corn, spooning over the leche de tigre.

tips.t: Marinate for just 2 minutes: lime cures fish fast, and if you wait it turns rubbery.
Use ají limo or rocoto from a Latin shop instead of the chili for true Peruvian heat.
Serve it with an ice-cold pisco sour, as in Lima's cevicherías.

title: Cá kho tộ, caramelised clay-pot mackerel
intro: Mackerel slowly cooked in caramel and fish sauce until the sauce is dark and sticky.

steps.t: Cut the mackerel into 4 cm steaks, rinse in salted water and pat dry. Chop the shallots and garlic.
Marinate the fish with the fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, the pepper and half the chopped aromatics for 20 minutes in the fridge.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: In a clay pot or small heavy pan heat the oil and remaining sugar until it becomes a deep amber caramel.
steps.label: Caramel

steps.t: Add the rest of the aromatics and straight away the fish in a single layer, then pour the marinade over.
Add water to come halfway up, add the chilies and bring to a boil. Cook uncovered on the lowest heat for 30 minutes, basting the fish.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Turn up the heat for 5 minutes until the sauce is thick and dark, turning the steaks gently once.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Scatter with spring onions and pepper and bring the pot to the table with hot steamed rice.

tips.t: Never stir: tilt the pot and spoon the sauce over the fish so the steaks stay whole.
In Vietnam it's often made with catfish: salmon steaks work well too.
Serve with sliced cucumber and plenty of rice: the salty sauce is meant to season it.

title: Samkeh harra, spicy tahini fish
intro: Baked sea bass smothered in tahini sauce with cilantro, chili and walnuts.

ing.n: whole sea bass, about 500 g each, cleaned

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220 °C. Score the fish 2 or 3 times on each side and season inside and out with salt, cumin, oil and half a lemon's juice.
Lay them in an oiled tray and bake at 220 °C for 20 minutes, until the flesh by the bone is white.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Meanwhile whisk the tahini with the juice of one lemon, the water and a pinch of salt into a sauce as smooth as thick cream.
In a pan fry the sliced onion in 2 tbsp oil until golden, then add the chopped garlic, chili and half the cilantro.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Pour in the tahini sauce and stir over low heat until it just thickens. Don't let it boil.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Spoon the sauce over the fish, scatter with chopped walnuts and return to the oven for 8 minutes, until bubbling at the edges.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Finish with the remaining cilantro and serve hot or at room temperature, with lemon wedges.

tips.t: With 4 sea bream or cod fillets, 12 minutes in the oven before the sauce is enough.
If the tahini sauce gets too thick or grainy, loosen it with a splash of hot water.
In Lebanon toasted pine nuts are also used instead of, or with, the walnuts.

title: Fish tagine with chermoula
intro: Fish marinated in herbs and spices, gently cooked over potatoes, peppers and olives.

steps.t: Make the chermoula: finely chop the cilantro, parsley and garlic and mix with paprika, cumin, chili, lemon juice, 6 tbsp oil and salt.
Spread half the chermoula over the fish and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Marinade

steps.t: Meanwhile slice the potatoes 5 mm thick, cut the peppers into strips, and thinly slice the tomatoes and the unwaxed lemon.
Spread the potatoes in a wide lidded pan, toss with the rest of the chermoula, add peppers and water. Cover and cook over medium-low heat.
steps.label: Potatoes

oven.t: Spread potatoes, remaining chermoula, peppers and water in a baking dish; cover with foil and bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.

steps.t: Lay the fish on the nearly tender potatoes, cover with tomatoes, olives and lemon and drizzle with the last oil. Cover and cook until it flakes.
steps.label: Fish

oven.t: Top with the fish, tomatoes, olives and lemon, drizzle with oil and bake covered at 200 °C for 20 minutes.

steps.t: Turn off the heat, rest for 5 minutes, scatter with cilantro and serve in the pan with bread.

tips.t: No tagine needed: a wide pan with a lid works, and the potatoes underneath protect the fish.
Wedges of preserved lemon from Moroccan shops give the sauce its classic perfume.
Serve with khobz to mop up the chermoula sauce.

title: Qing zheng yu, steamed sea bass
intro: Whole sea bass steamed, then dressed with ginger, spring onion and sizzling oil.

ing.n: sea bass, about 500 g each, gutted
f: sea bass, about 500 g each, gutted

steps.t: Pat the fish dry, make 2 or 3 diagonal cuts on each side and rub with the wine. Put half the sliced ginger inside and underneath.
Cut the rest of the ginger and the green part of the spring onions into very fine strips; soak in cold water so they curl.
Lay the fish on a plate and steam, covered, over high heat until the flesh near the bone is white and flakes away.
steps.label: Steam

oven.t: Wrap the fish in a foil parcel with the wine and bake at 200 °C for 18 minutes.

steps.t: Meanwhile warm the soy, sugar and water in a small pan until the sugar dissolves.
Pour off the cooking liquid, discard the cooked ginger, move the fish to a warm platter and top with the drained strips.
Heat the oil until smoking and pour it, sizzling, over the strips. Pour the sauce around the fish and finish with coriander.

tips.t: Don't salt the fish before steaming: the soy goes on at the end and the flesh stays silky.
Use tamari instead of soy sauce to make the dish gluten-free.

title: Hamsi tava, Turkish fried anchovies
intro: Anchovies dredged in cornmeal and fried in a sunburst, Black Sea style: crisp and golden.

steps.t: Clean the anchovies: pull off the head along with the guts, open the belly and lift out the spine, leaving the tail. Rinse.
Drain them in a colander, then pat them very dry with paper towel: they must be dry.
Mix the cornmeal and salt in a wide dish, dredge the anchovies and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan to 180 °C: a pinch of cornmeal should sizzle at once.
Arrange the anchovies in a sunburst, tails to the centre, and fry for 2½ minutes, until golden and crisp underneath.
steps.label: First side

airfryer.t: Lay the anchovies in a single layer in the basket, brush with oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 6 minutes.

steps.t: Flip the whole sunburst using a plate, like a frittata, and fry for 2 more minutes.
steps.label: Second side

airfryer.t: Turn them one by one and cook for 3 more minutes, until golden and crisp.

steps.t: Drain on paper, salt and serve at once with sliced red onion, parsley and lemon wedges.

tips.t: Dry the anchovies thoroughly: less water means less spitting and a crisper crust.
On the Black Sea they come with cornbread (mısır ekmeği) and a rocket and onion salad.

title: Garides saganaki (prawns with feta)
intro: Prawns in an ouzo-scented tomato sauce under a layer of melting feta.

steps.t: Peel the prawns, leaving the tails on, and remove the dark vein with a toothpick.
In a wide pan soften the chopped onion in the oil, then add the garlic and chili for 1 minute.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes, oregano and salt and simmer until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Nestle the prawns in the sauce, pour in the ouzo and cook, turning, until they turn pink.
steps.label: Prawns

steps.t: Crumble the feta over the top, cover and let it soften over low heat.
steps.label: Feta

oven.t: Transfer to a clay dish, crumble the feta over and bake at 200 °C for 8 minutes.

steps.t: Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve sizzling, with bread to mop up the sauce.

tips.t: No ouzo? Use a splash of dry white wine and a pinch of fennel seeds.
Take them off when the prawns are pink and C-shaped: an O shape means overcooked.

title: Meen curry, Kerala fish curry
intro: Fish gently cooked in coconut milk, soured with tamarind and fragrant with curry leaves.

steps.t: Cut the fish into 5 cm pieces, rub with salt and a pinch of turmeric and leave to season.
steps.label: Fish

steps.t: Meanwhile heat the coconut oil in a wide pan, let the mustard and fenugreek seeds pop, then add the curry leaves.
steps.label: Seeds

steps.t: Add the sliced onion, chopped garlic and ginger and split chilies; cook until the onion is golden.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Lower the heat, stir in turmeric, chili and coriander for 1 minute, then the chopped tomato until it breaks down.
steps.label: Tomato

steps.t: Dissolve the tamarind in the water, pour it in with half the coconut milk, salt and bring to a simmer.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Lay the fish in a single layer and cook gently without stirring, shaking the pan now and then.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and heat for 2 minutes without boiling.
steps.label: Coconut

steps.t: Turn off the heat and let it rest covered so the fish soaks up the sauce. Serve with white rice.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Kerala cooks use kudampuli, Malabar tamarind from Indian shops, for a sharper, smoky sauce.
Shake the pan instead of stirring with a spoon so the fish stays in whole pieces.
It's even better the next day: reheat gently without letting it boil.

title: Pulpo a la gallega, Galician octopus
intro: Tender octopus on boiled potatoes with coarse salt, pimentón and plenty of olive oil.

ing.n: sweet pimentón de la Vera (smoked paprika)

steps.t: If frozen, thaw the octopus in the fridge for 24 hours. Rinse it well under running water.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the bay leaf, no salt. Holding the head, dip the octopus in 3 times for 3 seconds.
Lower it in fully and, once it's back to the boil, cook over medium heat until a skewer slides easily into the thickest part.
steps.label: Octopus

pressure.t: In a pressure cooker with 1 litre of water: seal and cook for 15 minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: Turn off the heat and leave the octopus in the water for 10 more minutes, then lift it out.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: In the same water cook the peeled potatoes, in 1.5 cm slices, until tender.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Meanwhile snip the tentacles with scissors into 1.5 cm rounds.
Lay the potatoes on a wooden board with the octopus on top; sprinkle with coarse salt and pimentón and drizzle generously with oil.

tips.t: Frozen octopus is more tender: freezing breaks the fibres, just like beating it on the rocks used to.
Mix a pinch of hot pimentón into the sweet one, as Galician pulperías do.
Serve on a wooden board with bread and a chilled Albariño from Rías Baixas.

title: Moules marinières
intro: Mussels steamed open with shallots, white wine, butter and parsley, the French way.

steps.t: Rinse the mussels under cold water, pull off the beards and discard any broken ones or open ones that don't close when tapped.
In a large, deep pot melt half the butter and soften the chopped shallots over low heat without letting them brown.
steps.label: Shallots

steps.t: Pour in the wine, add the thyme and bay leaf and boil hard for 1 minute.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Tip in the mussels, cover and cook over high heat, shaking the pot a couple of times, until they have all opened.
steps.label: Mussels

steps.t: Discard any that stayed shut, add the remaining butter, the parsley and some black pepper and toss.
Serve straight away in deep bowls with the juices and baguette for mopping up.

tips.t: Don't salt, and use a big pot: the mussels should sit in two or three layers so they open together.
Moules à la crème: stir in 100 ml cream at the end and let it bubble for 1 minute.
In northern France and Belgium they come with fries: moules-frites.
